scope: LIVE // EARTH Weather Live Art card only

canvas.footprintInterpretation: visual composition and scene envelope, not literal non-paper pixel coverage

visualIdentity.style: minimalist Japanese-inspired monochromatic ink line art
markMaking: simple expressive outlines and recognisable silhouettes
objects suggested rather than fully described

strokeHierarchy.implementationNote: The current renderer has no per-path strokeWidth property. Encode line thickness geometrically as narrow closed ribbon paths.

weatherColourRule.principle: Weather changes the subject and its details, not the overall colour treatment.

clear: few birds or crisp simple details
storm: few decisive cloud or rain marks

progressiveReplay.revealRule: Replay progressively reveals the paths array in stored order.
progressiveReplay.authoringRequirement: Order the paths array by the approved artwork-specific drawing stages; never sort or shuffle it after authoring.
rendererLimitations: No semantic drawing-stage labels are interpreted by the renderer.
No named stage pauses or stage timing are supported.
No per-path strokeWidth metadata is supported.
Completed paths are filled closed shapes; line-like marks must be narrow closed shapes.
The artwork plan documents intent; actual Replay sequence is determined by paths array order.

workflow: Read the human guide, this JSON, active reference and current catalogue.
Use the weather condition explicitly selected by the user; never substitute another condition.
Work on one scene at a time; no unrequested batches or collages.
Propose and obtain approval for one scene composition before asset production.
Write a unique artwork-specific plan with exact ordered stages and stroke weights.
Author encoded path data in that exact order.
Review the 70/30 breathing-space balance and small-card legibility.
Validate asset schema, palette indices, coordinate bounds, IDs, and path order.
Update the catalogue without changing existing IDs or renderer behaviour.
Package and verify; do not claim device success before user testing.

artworkPlans.title: A Rainy Tea Afternoon
artworkPlans.story: A quiet tea moment by a rain-streaked window, with a distant pavilion beyond the hills.

sequence.instruction: Establish the door/window frame and sill first with strong, confident thick structural strokes.
Draw the flowing main branch, then a few selected leaves. Thick branch strokes; medium leaf shapes.
Add long, elegant, restrained lines for the distant hills. Medium-to-thin weight; keep the horizon quiet.
Reveal the small distant house/pavilion with only necessary roof and building outlines. Medium weight; no micro-detail.
Draw the kettle and teacup carefully as the focal still-life objects. Medium outlines and only a few defining details; leave interiors mostly paper.
Add the red sun, selected red maple leaves and intended tiny red accents last. No extra red decoration.

artworkPlans.instruction: Do not invent or register a clear-weather drawing plan until the user approves the specific subject and composition.
